title: An iron rod shot through his head

post.youtube_title: An Iron Rod Shot Through His Skull. He Lived. 😳 #shorts
post.caption: In 1848, a 6 kg iron rod blasted through Phineas Gage's head. He was talking within minutes, and his case changed what we know about the brain 🧠
post.pinned_comment: Would you have kept the rod? 👇

sources: Harlow JM (1848, 1868), Boston Medical and Surgical Journal / Publications of the Massachusetts Medical Society: on 13 September 1848 near Cavendish, Vermont, a tamping iron 3 ft 7 in long and 13.25 lb passed through the left side of Phineas Gage's face and out of the top of his head; he spoke within minutes and rode an ox cart sitting up; friends said he was 'no longer Gage'; Harlow wrote that the iron was his constant companion for the rest of his life
Macmillan M (2000), An Odd Kind of Fame (MIT Press): the iron landed about 80 ft (25 m) away; Gage later worked as a stagecoach driver in Chile for about seven years
Gage's skull and the tamping iron are on display at the Warren Anatomical Museum, Harvard Medical School

beats.text: In {1848|eighteen forty-eight}, an iron rod shot straight through a man's *skull*.

beats.text: He didn't die. He was *talking* within minutes.
His name was Phineas Gage, a railroad foreman in Vermont, blasting rock to make way for the tracks.
He was packing explosive powder into a hole with an iron rod, when a spark set it *off*.

elements.markup: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 1000 80'><defs><linearGradient id='m' x1='0' y1='0' x2='0' y2='1'><stop offset='0' stop-color='#3a3a3a'/><stop offset='0.45' stop-color='#e8e8e8'/><stop offset='1' stop-color='#2a2a2a'/></linearGradient></defs><path d='M20 25 L900 25 L990 40 L900 55 L20 55 Q5 40 20 25 Z' fill='url(#m)' stroke='#1a1a1a' stroke-width='3'/></svg>

beats.text: The rod was over a meter long, and weighed about *six* kilograms.

elements.markup: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 1000 80'><defs><linearGradient id='m' x1='0' y1='0' x2='0' y2='1'><stop offset='0' stop-color='#3a3a3a'/><stop offset='0.45' stop-color='#e8e8e8'/><stop offset='1' stop-color='#2a2a2a'/></linearGradient></defs><path d='M20 25 L900 25 L990 40 L900 55 L20 55 Q5 40 20 25 Z' fill='url(#m)' stroke='#1a1a1a' stroke-width='3'/></svg>

beats.text: It went in under his left cheekbone, passed behind his eye, and flew out the top of his *head*.

beats.text: It landed about {25|twenty-five} meters away. Then Gage rode back to town in an ox cart, sitting *upright*.

elements.markup: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 1000 80'><defs><linearGradient id='m' x1='0' y1='0' x2='0' y2='1'><stop offset='0' stop-color='#3a3a3a'/><stop offset='0.45' stop-color='#e8e8e8'/><stop offset='1' stop-color='#2a2a2a'/></linearGradient></defs><path d='M20 25 L900 25 L990 40 L900 55 L20 55 Q5 40 20 25 Z' fill='url(#m)' stroke='#1a1a1a' stroke-width='3'/></svg>

beats.text: He survived. But his friends said he was no longer *Gage*.
Reports say the reliable foreman became impatient, unpredictable, and full of *swear* words.
His case helped show that the front of the brain shapes who we *are*.

beats.text: And there's a twist. He later moved to Chile, and drove a {stagecoach|stage coach} for *years*.
Today, his skull and that rod are on display at *Harvard*.

beats.text: He kept that rod for the rest of his life. Talk about a *souvenir*.
